title: Off-duty Border Patrol agent Abel Garza charged with murder in fatal Texana Street stabbing
excerpt: Abel Garza, 30, an off-duty Border Patrol agent, was charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, after the Oct. 28 Texana Street stabbing, KGNS and the Laredo Morning Times reported.
content:
Abel Garza, 30, an off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent, was charged with murder, a first-degree felony, in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, according to KGNS, which reported the charge on October 28. The Laredo Morning Times also reported the murder charge.

Garza was also charged with two counts of endangering a child and two counts of abandonment of a child, all second-degree felonies, KGNS reported, and he remains held on bonds totaling $1.5 million, according to the Times. Two children were found safe at the home, KGNS reported.

This is a development in the case Webb Watch reported earlier on October 28, when Laredo Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez confirmed that the detained man is a Border Patrol agent. Police are calling the case Laredo's sixth homicide of 2026.

According to the Times, police responded to calls about a domestic disturbance at about 2:45 a.m. on Wednesday, October 28, in the 5500 block of Texana Street. A police drone pilot saw a vehicle leaving the area, and officers intercepted it. Landeros was found alive in the rear floorboard of the vehicle with multiple stab wounds, was taken to a hospital, and later died. KGNS placed the incident just before 3 a.m. near Texana and Nocona, off Cuatro Vientos, and reported that CBP said Garza was arrested at 6 a.m., with its Office of Professional Responsibility reviewing the case.

The Times also reported prior arrests for Garza: booked January 15 on aggravated assault with a deadly weapon involving a family or household member, released January 17 on a $100,000 bond; and booked February 20 on unlawful restraint, interfering with an emergency request, and violating a bond or protective order, released February 21 on bonds totaling $15,000.

Garza is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law on the current charges. Webb Watch will update this story when court records release further charging details.

Update — Friday, Nov. 6: An eight-page search warrant affidavit detailing the investigation into Landeros' death has shed more light on the night she was stabbed, according to KGNS. The affidavit says neighbors called police after a blood-covered man knocked on doors asking for help, and a police drone spotted two men running before officers followed an SUV to the 1600 block of Latigo Loop, where Landeros was found bleeding in the back of the vehicle. Garza told police he saw messages on his wife's phone, asked her to separate, and said she began stabbing herself with a kitchen knife, according to the affidavit, and said he did not call 911 because he did not know where his phone was. A family member called police claiming Garza confessed to killing his wife, and Garza's father reportedly confirmed the confession to police, according to the report. Investigators are also looking into the couple's previous domestic-dispute history.

Update — Saturday, Nov. 7: A search-warrant affidavit filed October 29 and presented at a court hearing Friday, November 6, lays out conflicting accounts of the morning Landeros died, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The affidavit was filed to obtain a DNA sample from Garza for comparison with evidence collected at the scene. It says the couple's 13-year-old daughter called 911 at about 6:45 a.m. on October 27 after Garza woke her and said Landeros was hurt. The daughter told investigators she found Landeros on the bathroom floor with a knife nearby and a sheet covering her body, and said Garza told her Landeros had stabbed herself and was not dead. She also said Garza told her Landeros had attacked him first and he had stabbed her in self-defense, and that she heard no struggle before Garza woke her — only Garza screaming Landeros' name from the bathroom. Garza told police Landeros attacked him with a knife, he took the knife from her and stabbed her in self-defense, then called 911. The affidavit says his statements to police differed from the daughter's account about what happened before she was woken and the sequence of events. An autopsy by the Webb County Medical Examiner's Office found Landeros died from a single stab wound to the chest. Garza remains charged with murder and four counts of abandoning or endangering a child, held on bonds totaling $1.5 million, and remained in custody at the Webb County Jail as of Saturday morning, November 7. Garza is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.
